title: Greetings, and thanks for all the fish

posts.author: FWT
posts.body:
Hi everybody, I'm new to this forum but not to RPG Maker, which I discovered in 2001. I live in France, and I've never quite gotten used to game-making software other than RM2K and RM2K3. My goal for next year is to upgrade my skills and dive into the magnificent world of MV.
I'll be glad to discuss with other enthusiasts.
I'm currently putting the finishing touches on my project
A Tale of Yu
, a management-adventure RPG where you run a hot springs inn similar to a Japanese onsen, except that it welcomes RPG monsters and adventurers in an attempt to maintain peace in the kingdom.

posts.author: Tortletalk
posts.body:
Hi!  Welcome
Your game sounds interesting!  Does it have a feature were you have to stop the guys spying on the girls (or vice versa?) in true anime fashion?

posts.author: FWT
posts.body:
Hi Tortletalk ! Thanks for your message !
In
A Tale of Yu
, baths are mixed because I wanted to establish from the beginning that, in-game, the society is fully gender-equal, with sexual assault being nonexistent, and that particular trope wouldn’t be used. However, there is still a separation between monsters and humans baths, with some characters hinting that they’d like to cross this boundary—not for peeking, but simply to try a new type of water (or lava. Or acid.). I wanted this to underline how the society struggles to achieve full coexistence between humans and other species, and how we often build walls where none are needed.
